memory_update.text: PLTR should remain the reference benchmark for enterprise and government AI workflow deployment, but its high attention and mega-cap status make it unsuitable for the underfollowed lane.

CCCS is a credible underfollowed vertical AI/data workflow candidate because its insurance-claims network, historical data, and P&C workflow penetration may be difficult for generic AI vendors to replicate.

DFIN is a credible underfollowed regulated-workflow candidate because AI-assisted SEC filing, disclosure, fund reporting, and capital-markets document automation sit inside compliance-gated workflows.
MITK belongs in speculative_shadow rather than core underfollowed until evidence confirms AI/deepfake fraud is producing measurable incremental revenue rather than just competitive/R&D pressure.

Next pass should verify current market caps, analyst coverage, ARR or software mix, customer concentration, AI-specific revenue contribution, and whether each company has durable proprietary data rights rather than generic AI feature exposure.

node: Vertical AI software, proprietary data, and workflow automation
summary: Layer 1B expansion focused on US-listed public companies tied to vertical AI deployment, proprietary workflow data, regulated software, and compliance-gated automation. The reference lane is represented by Palantir as the obvious high-attention AI workflow platform. The underfollowed lane emphasizes firms with narrower domain datasets or regulated workflows: insurance claims, SEC/capital-markets compliance, and identity/fraud verification. These are not recommendations; they are candidates for deeper evidence checks.
